**No.** Krishna Kale can receive hall tickets for four of the five courses, but not for **CS102 – Engineering Physics** because the attendance requirement is not met.

| Course (code) | Attendance | Exam‑fee status | Eligibility |
|---------------|------------|----------------|-------------|
| CS101 – Engineering Mathematics I | 79.6 % [SQL] | paid, ₹0 due [SQL] | ✅ meets ≥75 % |
| **CS102 – Engineering Physics** | **73.5 %** [SQL] | paid, ₹0 due [SQL] | ❌ below 75 % |
| CS103 – Programming in C | 85.6 % [SQL] | paid, ₹0 due [SQL] | ✅ meets ≥75 % |
| CS104 – Basic Electrical Engineering | 77.2 % [SQL] | paid, ₹0 due [SQL] | ✅ meets ≥75 % |
| CS105 – Programming Lab I | 77.8 % [SQL] | paid, ₹0 due [SQL] | ✅ meets ≥75 % |

**Why CS102 blocks a full hall ticket**

* Hall tickets are issued only when (1) the examination fee for the term is fully paid **and** (2) the student meets the attendance requirement for each listed course [Doc: Examination & Attendance Rules 2026-27 §5 Hall tickets].  
* The fee condition is satisfied for all courses (outstanding balance ₹0) [SQL].  
* The attendance rule requires **≥ 75 %** in each registered course [Doc: Examination & Attendance Rules 2026-27 §2 Minimum attendance]. CS102 has 73.5 %, which is below this threshold.  
* The student is not detained (attendance > 65 %) [Doc: Examination & Attendance Rules 2026-27 §4 Detention], but detention is not required for eligibility; the 75 % minimum still applies.

**Result:** Hall tickets can be issued for CS101, CS103, CS104, and CS105, but not for CS102. Therefore, Krishna Kale cannot obtain a hall ticket for **all** end‑semester exams this term.
sql: SELECT c.course_code, c.title, e.attendance_pct, f.component, (f.amount_due - f.amount_paid) AS outstanding_balance, f.status AS fee_status FROM enrollments AS e JOIN courses AS c ON e.course_id = c.course_id LEFT JOIN fee_ledger AS f ON e.student_id = f.student_id AND f.component = 'exam' WHERE e.student_id = 'S2026CS003' AND e.term = '2026-ODD' LIMIT 200
